tools.name: find_businesses
tools.description: Search the DouxProcess Directory for US businesses by what the person needs (roofer, electrician, insurance agency...) and where (a city and state, a ZIP, or a state). Returns the matches in the published ranking order with license, how it was checked, phone, website and listing page. covered=false

tools.name: get_business
tools.description: One business's details: licenses with their basis (issuer_file = matched against the issuer's own published file on checked_at; stated = given by the business, not yet matched, send the person to source_url), contact, whether it takes requests, and its own agent addresses (MCP and A2A).

tools.name: verify_license
tools.description: Look up a license by number, business name or phone and say which listings carry it and how it was checked. When nothing matches, tell the person to check the issuer's own lookup; never say a license is valid without a match.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: Every category with its id, NAICS 2022 code, plain name, Google Business Profile names, how many listings it has, and whether requests for it are sent (health is listed but never routed).

tools.name: ask
tools.description: Ask in plain words ('licensed electrician near 92101 who does EV chargers') and get a short answer built only from listings, plus the businesses it rests on, in the published order. Same rules as find_businesses: no ranking or recommendation language, coverage stated honestly.

tools.name: request_contact
tools.description: Sends the person's request to the ONE business they chose, so it can reply to them. Only claimed listings take requests, and health businesses never do. Before calling, show the person this sentence and get their agreement: 'I agree that DouxProcess sends my name, my contact details and this request

tools.name: request_service
tools.description: Open the request form for one business the person chose (ChatGPT local services Get Quote). The form shows the consent sentence and sends only when the person ticks it. For a business that does not take requests it shows the business's own phone and website.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "request_contact" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Sends the person's request to the ONE business they chose, so it can reply to them. Only claimed listings take requests, and health businesses never do. Before …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "request_contact" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
